title: Stratify the train/test split for model-based embedding drift
body:
## Problem

ModelDriftMethod creates a binary source label for reference/current embeddings, then uses an unstratified 50/50 split. Even when both populations contain at least two rows, the fixed random split can leave the training set with one class. For example, reference/current sizes 2/8 and 3/4 raise SGDClassifier's single-class error. Training the classifier and evaluating its ROC AUC both require the source classes to remain represented.

## Change

Stratify train_test_split by the existing source labels, preserving the 50/50 ratio, shuffle setting, random seed, classifier, and thresholds. This change is independent of the separate fix for using an embedding dimension named target.

## Validation

- 10 new tests on the upstream base: 5 failed, 5 passed.
- Fixed tests plus the existing embedding-drift Report test: 11 passed on CPU.
- Cases cover small imbalanced samples in both directions, a balanced control, bootstrap and fixed-threshold decisions, an explicit stratified SGD/ROC reference, and a real Report integration control.
- The tests restore the caller's NumPy random state so the existing bootstrap behavior cannot contaminate other tests.
- Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

Stratification can change numeric scores on existing datasets because it changes which rows enter each split. This does not provide a statistically reliable drift estimate from arbitrarily small datasets: each population must have enough rows for both splits. The Report plotting layer's independent t-SNE/KDE sample requirements are unchanged; the Report control uses a sufficient sample size.
